commits.edited_message:
Reject truncated UTF-8 char data in Mat_VarRead5

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/issues/342

Bytes 0xF8-0xFF are not continuation bytes and do not start a
multi-byte sequence. Count each as one character so the decoded
length still matches the array dimensions and Mat_VarCreate, which
advances one byte when Mat_Utf8SeqLen returns 0.
commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/mat5.c b/src/mat5.c
index 04d071a..06964c2 100644
--- a/src/mat5.c
+++ b/src/mat5.c
@@ -3519,9 +3519,12 @@ Mat_VarReadNumeric5(mat_t *mat, matvar_t *matvar, void *data, size_t N)
  *
  * Walks @c nbytes bytes of UTF-8 data, verifying that every multi-byte
  * sequence is complete and that the total number of decoded characters
- * equals @c expected. Used by the reader to reject malformed character data
- * before it is handed back to the caller, which may re-wrap the buffer with
- * Mat_VarCreate (which trusts the buffer bounds while recomputing @c nbytes).
+ * equals @c expected. Bytes 0xF8-0xFF are not continuation bytes and do not
+ * start a multi-byte sequence; each is counted as one character so the
+ * decoded length can still match the array dimensions. Used by the reader to
+ * reject malformed character data before it is handed back to the caller,
+ * which may re-wrap the buffer with Mat_VarCreate (which trusts the buffer
+ * bounds while recomputing @c nbytes).
  *
  * @ingroup mat_internal
  * @param data pointer to the UTF-8 data
@@ -3536,7 +3539,11 @@ ValidateUtf8CharData(const mat_uint8_t *data, size_t nbytes, size_t expected)
     size_t nchars = 0;
 
     while ( i < nbytes ) {
-        const size_t len = Mat_Utf8SeqLen(data[i]);
+        size_t len;
+        if ( data[i] >= 0xF8 )
+            len = 1;
+        else
+            len = Mat_Utf8SeqLen(data[i]);
         if ( len == 0 || i + len > nbytes )
             return MATIO_E_FILE_FORMAT_VIOLATION;
         i += len;

commits.edited_message:
Fix testcase failures in big endian machines

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/372

Count bytes 0xF8-0xFF as two-byte sequences in Mat_Utf8SeqLen. Those
values are not continuation bytes; treating them as length 0 made
Mat_VarCreate and Mat_PrintData consume only the first octet and
decode the following octet as its own character.

---------

Co-authored-by: tbeu <tbeu@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/mat.c b/src/mat.c
index c46790a..1c58a4b 100644
--- a/src/mat.c
+++ b/src/mat.c
@@ -456,8 +456,9 @@ ClassType2DataType(enum matio_classes class_type)
 /** @brief Returns the length of a UTF-8 sequence for a lead byte
  *
  * Determines the number of bytes (1-4) that make up a UTF-8 code point whose
- * first byte is @c c. Returns 0 for bytes that cannot start a valid UTF-8
- * sequence (continuation bytes and bytes 0xF8-0xFF).
+ * first byte is @c c. Continuation bytes return 0. Bytes 0xF8-0xFF are not
+ * continuation bytes; count them as a two-byte sequence so callers consume
+ * the following octet with the lead byte.
  *
  * @ingroup MAT
  * @param c first byte of the UTF-8 sequence
@@ -474,6 +475,8 @@ Mat_Utf8SeqLen(mat_uint8_t c)
         return 3;
     else if ( (c & 0xF8) == 0xF0 )
         return 4;
+    else if ( c >= 0xF8 )
+        return 2;
     else
         return 0;
 }

coupling:
ValidateUtf8CharData (9d5bb8d) and Mat_Utf8SeqLen (9c74e17) disagree about how many bytes one 0xF8-0xFF octet occupies, and neither commit contains both sides.

9d5bb8d counts each such octet as one character inside ValidateUtf8CharData and does not call Mat_Utf8SeqLen for it. At that commit the helper still returns 0, and Mat_VarCreate advances one byte on a 0 return (len == 0 ? 1 : len), so the buffer the reader returns is exactly what a later Mat_VarCreate copies. Truncated multi-byte sequences and continuation bytes are still rejected. Read alone, the new check matches the creator.

9c74e17 changes Mat_Utf8SeqLen so those bytes return 2. Mat_VarCreate and Mat_PrintData in the same file consume that return value, and Mat_PrintData still refuses to read past nbytes, so the diff is consistent with the callers it touches. It does not change the validator, which keeps forcing length 1.

The overrun appears only when both are present. Mat_VarRead5 accepts a 1x1 miUTF8 array whose payload is a single 0xFF (first commit) and allocates one byte. Mat_VarCreate, given that public matvar, walks one character with the helper, sets nbytes to 2 (second commit), and memcpy's two bytes out of the one-byte allocation. Either edit by itself keeps the lengths equal: without the validator special case the reader drops the buffer and the re-wrap is not reached; without the longer sequence length Mat_VarCreate copies the single byte that was allocated. Repairing it means making those two lengths the same. Updating only the truncation check, the comment, or the big-endian tag swap in one commit leaves the other commit's length in place, and the copy still reads one byte past the buffer.
